subject: SLA exception request: fallback-and-pin rollout policy for new model variant
messages:
From: Amy Carter <amy.carter@novahealth.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@novahealth.com
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary SLA exception for model swap (fallback plan proposed)

Hi Jonas / Dylan,

Quick context: Nova is preparing to swap our online reranker to the v2.1 quantized variant you onboarded last week. Internal perf tests look promising for cost, but we saw a 20-30ms median latency bump and occasional p95 spikes during long sequences in our staging runs. Given our active production traffic and existing SLOs, we need to request a short SLA exception window during the rollout unless we can guarantee an automated mitigation.

What we propose (high level):
- A canary (10% traffic) for 24 hours with aggressive monitoring.
- Automatic fallback to the pinned v2.0 version if p95 latency or error rate thresholds are breached.
- Pinning of the stable model for the remaining 90% of traffic until canary completes.

Can Redwood confirm you can implement automatic fallback + model pinning as an SLA mitigation and, if so, whether you can commit to telemetry/incident hooks so we (Nova SRE) can see the rollback triggers? If automatic fallback is not possible, we will need a formal SLA exception and credits for the window.

Thanks — would like to schedule a short sync if necessary.

Amy Carter
SRE Lead, Nova Health Systems
amy.carter@novahealth.com
Attachment: test-run-summary.csv (CSV stub)

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Carter <amy.carter@novahealth.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA exception for model swap (fallback plan proposed)

Amy — thanks for the clear ask and for the staging data. Short answer: yes, we can run the rollout with the mitigations you described, and we recommend an automatic fallback circuit combined with model version pinning as the primary SLA protection.

Proposed operational plan (summary):
- Canary window: start at 5% traffic for 4 hours, then 10% for 20 hours if stable. We prefer the conservative ramp.
- Fallback policy: automatic fallback to pinned v2.0 when any of the following triggers hit for the canary slice over a 5-minute rolling window:
  * p95 latency > 350ms (user-facing inference path)
  * error rate > 0.5% (5xxs or stream terminations)
  * request queue length or token generation stalls > 2x baseline
- Pinning: production route will be pinned to v2.0 for non-canary traffic until canary passes. Pinning will be implemented via route-level model_version tag in the routing policy.
- Monitoring & observability: we'll expose an SRE-facing dashboard (token-level latency, p95/p99, errors) and a webhook that posts rollback events to your PagerDuty channel and to the Drive audit log.
- Rollback semantics: rollback is immediate for the canary slice and will not automatically unpin the production route — unpin requires manual approval from Nova or a scheduled automated reattempt.

Attached are the fallback playbook and a suggested traffic schedule. Please confirm the thresholds above or propose alternatives. Once we have agreement I can open an exception form with Billing if you want the event captured as an SLA exception in the contract.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Attachments: fallback_playbook.pdf (PDF), canary_traffic_schedule.xlsx (XLSX)

Amy — quick commercial note from my side: if Nova wants the SLA exception documented (credits if fallback doesn't prevent an SLO breach), we need a signed addendum. I can prepare an SLA-exception-form (attached draft) that captures the exact window and credit calculation (pro-rated by tokens/requests).

Operationally Jonas' conservative ramp looks good. Suggest we start at 5% for 6 hours to minimize exposure, then 10% for 18 hours contingent on green metrics. Also propose that we keep daily checkpoints (end-of-day status email) during the first 72 hours after the canary completes.

Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 15:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA exception for model swap (fallback plan proposed)

Technical follow-up from infra/runtime: we can implement the fallback and pinning as described. A few implementation details and caveats to call out: 
- Circuit-breaker thresholds: we'll implement a rolling-window evaluator (5m) that triggers a hard route switch for the canary. The routing switch is atomic for the canary pool.
- Telemetry: rollback events will emit an audit event to the Drive link and will also post to your PagerDuty channel. We'll include the raw request_id samples for any rollback window for post-mortem.
- Model pinning: we use the model_version tag and keep the pinned artifact immutable. Reverting the pin is a manual operation from your SRE or a scheduled safe reattempt.
- KV cache concerns: switching between quantized variants can cause cache misses that temporarily increase latency. To minimize, we'll warm the KV cache for the canary nodes before traffic hits them and use a short grace period for cold-cache metrics (we'll exclude the first 10 minutes when evaluating p95 for rollback).
- Edge case: if the fallback itself fails due to capacity constraints on v2.0, we'll initiate a multi-node fallback (route traffic to a dedicated backup pool). That scenario should only happen if v2.0 capacity is saturated — we'll surface it immediately.

I've logged technical details in INF-2145 and attached a mini-playbook to the ticket. Let me know if you want the thresholds tuned (I can lower p95 to 320ms or tighten error rate).

Vivek Kulkarni
Engineering Manager, Inference Runtime, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Thanks — this looks good and reasonable. We approve the conservative ramp (5% -> 10%) and the automatic fallback rules as long as:
- Redwood confirms rollback webhook will include the raw request_ids for our internal correlation, and
- The SLA exception addendum is drafted with an explicit statement that if automatic fallback fails to prevent an SLO hit during the window, Nova will be eligible for credits per the addendum's formula.

Please share the signed addendum and confirm the start date/time for the canary. Prefer to start Monday at 09:00 PT.
